scope: Adversarial review of G4/G5 pool semantics, anonymous full-instance canonicalization and isolated Java worker architecture. No claim that Lean builds, Java implementation, dataset coverage or retrieval quality have passed.
blocker_resolution: Requires replayed CHECKED proof for the exact selected body occurrence and pinned trusted context, input, inventory and rules; missing or unrelated proof rejects admission.
Constructs both polarities under the same explicitly frozen scope profile and ignores original command scopes; provenance retains effective scope and attributes.

Captures the exact complete static universe, signature membership and all fields, including empty ones, using a single shared permutation, with numeric integers fixed and bounded failures producing no key.
Separates existence from enumeration termination and retains prior validated witnesses without inventing completeness after failures.
Includes a dependency token when retained facts or functions transitively invoke the target and evaluates in the exact original parsed world.
Uses dedicated subprocess isolation, private /tmp, strict framing and exact identity binding, while preserving captured binder slots.

new: backend/src/main/java/dev/allow/corpus/CorpusWorkerMain.java — strictly bounded, one-request framed child entry point; isolate protocol stdout and avoid Spring registration.

backend/src/main/java/dev/allow/corpus/CorpusRequest.java and CorpusResponse.java — immutable versioned request/response records, exact source and build identity, complete bounds, target occurrence, independent polarity statuses and immutable provenance.

backend/src/main/java/dev/allow/corpus/CorpusEngine.java — parse/admit static single module, construct both semantic queries with one profile, validate solutions in original world, and invoke incremental enumeration with hard limits.

backend/src/main/java/dev/allow/corpus/InstanceCanonicalizer.java — complete full-instance schema and globally shared atom bijection, lexicographic canonical encoding, safe budget outcomes; hashes only index exact bytes.
backend/src/main/java/dev/allow/corpus/PoolBuilder.java — distinct canonical members, witness validation and per-polarity evidence/status lifecycle, bounded and immutable.

backend/src/main/java/dev/allow/canonical/RetrievalContextEncoder.java and narrowly scoped capture facade — target-body marker, whole selected-command exclusion, retained dependency token, and proof binding from the same traversal while leaving v1 bytes unchanged.
backend/src/test/java/dev/allow/corpus/ — end-to-end worker, query polarity, proof binding, renaming/isomorphism, resource boundaries, frame validation and concurrent isolation fixtures.
implementation_file_plan.existing_changes: Only minimal additive canonical capture and sandbox launch/build wiring necessary for this worker. Preserve preexisting public request/results, egraph semantics, v1 bytes and ordinary solver behavior. Coordinate shared build/launcher edits with other owners.
implementation_file_plan.implementation_guard: Do not begin production edits until root announces the formal gate VERIFIED. Existing two clean builds must complete and exact propositions plus input hashes and review resolution must be audited independently; this review is not a formal gate verdict.

implementation_checks: Verify facts are conjoined exactly once in generated Alloy command semantics, including target-dependent facts and an inconsistent-facts fixture. Differentiate next() exhaustion from cutoff and preserve valid prior witnesses.

Test globally renamed instances and equal-degree nonisomorphic structures, integer semantics, empty fields, tuple ordering, atom and permutation limits, hash collisions by exact-byte comparison, and polarity/context mismatch rejection.

Use a target-free context traversal independent of original command content while retaining original-world target proof capture; reject if exact trusted occurrence cannot be replayed. Verify other bodies, facts and dependency changes affect compatibility.
Validate that timeout/kill or output overflow cannot become UNSAT, full completion or publishable evidence. Require both pools of N distinct complete validated members before vector eligibility.
limitations: The formal obligations describe an abstract policy; Alloy parser, translator, evaluator, instance projection, proof-binding adapter and solver remain trusted implementation components and require adversarial integration tests.
The reviewed spec does not prove corpus feasibility, embedding quality, or database readiness; these remain evidence-dependent later gates.
